summary: A personal essay by Rachel Nusbaum on Orchid Story, describing how a rejected graduate-school dream led her to question the "Work Hard and Achieve" belief. It then presents five common self-limiting beliefs women hold (no time for self, not knowing where to start, selfishness of self-care, being a victim of past events, and not being good enough), each paired with a suggested reframe to rewrite it.
one_line: Rachel Nusbaum's Orchid Story essay on five common self-limiting beliefs and how to rewrite them.
key_facts: The author was a senior and Division I college athlete with an almost perfect GPA who planned to attend graduate school for genetic counseling.
The author was denied by all 10 graduate schools to which she had applied.
The author's original mantra was "Work hard and you will achieve it."
The essay states that "what matters most is the journey because we have so little control over the outcome."
Belief 1 is "I don't have any time to focus on me," described as the queen of all self-limiting beliefs.
The essay suggests that every person has three minutes in their day to listen to a guided meditation or take a couple of deep breaths.
The essay recommends the Insight Timer app as a meditation tool.
Belief 2 is "I don't know where to start," and the essay advises: "Start anywhere, try anything."
Belief 3 is "It feels selfish to take time to work on myself," and the suggested reframe is "I serve best when my cup is full."
The essay attributes the negativity bias to human evolution, using the example of a tiger in the bushes that could eat you.
Belief 4 is "I feel like a victim of the negative experiences in my life," with the reframe "I've been through tough times and I'm a more resilient person because of it."
Belief 5 is "I'm not good enough," which the essay says is especially common for Achievers.
For Belief 5, the suggested reframe is "I am worthy simply by existing. I don't need to prove my worth."
The essay was published February 12, 2020 under the Personal Essay category and is tagged Self-limiting belief, Self-development, Rewrite your story, and Transformation.
